session_covered: US and European sessions of Thursday 22 October
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Thursday 22 October. Delayed from the early-morning run because sources conflicted; some figures are approximate or single-source, as footnoted.
footnotes: US index, VIX and gold figures are from Yahoo Finance's post-close snapshot; other outlets showed different Nasdaq (-2.07% to -2.87%) and Dow (-0.53% to -0.09%) moves, and Yahoo's levels reconcile with the prior closes. The 10-year yield is the US Treasury daily par yield (4.96% vs 5.13%). AUD/USD, Brent (reported "above US$113", +4%) and iron ore (grade not stated) are single-source from ABC News snapshots; gold was US$4,023 (-2.85%) in the same snapshot.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures point lower, but sources differ on size: ABC News had them -0.2% at 8,803 and Investing.com -0.67% at 8,785 (TradingView's +0.09% looks stale). Taking the midpoint, futures are down roughly 0.2-0.7% (level 8,785-8,803), implying an ASX 200 open about 40 points (-0.45%) lower, near 8,754 (approximate). The ASX 200 closed Thursday at 8,793.2, down 38.1 points (-0.43%), led lower by miners.

local_events: RBA Governor Bullock appears before parliament
Treasurer Chalmers speaks on business investment
what_moved: A tech and AI sell-off drove the session after Meta lifted its capex guidance and reported negative free cash flow: the Nasdaq had its worst day since June and the semiconductor index fell more than 6%. Oil jumped about 4% to a five-month high on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and US-Iran escalation fears, while a flight to quality pushed the 10-year yield below 5%. Sector-level S&P 500 returns were not available.

news.headline: AI capex worries hit tech.
news.summary: Meta fell about 7% after raising its 2026 capex range to US$135-145 billion, dragging Nvidia (-4%), AMD (-8%) and Micron (-6%).

news.headline: Brent at a five-month high.
news.summary: Crude settled above US$113/bbl after further Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and concerns about a US-Iran escalation.

news.headline: Treasury yields tumble.
news.summary: The 10-year par yield fell 17 bp to 4.96% and the 2-year 16 bp to 4.65% in a flight to quality.

news.headline: RBA signals possible hike.
news.summary: Deputy Governor Hauser put September headline CPI at 4% and hinted at a rate rise on Melbourne Cup Day.

news.headline: China stocks in a bear market.
news.summary: The CSI 300 fell 1.8% on Thursday, 20% below its June peak, and the Hang Seng Tech index fell as much as 5.3%.

news.headline: Chalmers flags softer growth.
news.summary: The Treasurer said higher rates and inflation are likely to mean softer growth and slightly higher unemployment, while touting a business investment upgrade.

news.headline: ASX 200 slips on miners.
news.summary: The index fell 0.43% to 8,793 Thursday; Fortescue lost 4.5%.

coming_up: US Federal Reserve meeting on 27-28 October (no projections); RBA decision expected on Melbourne Cup Day, Tuesday 3 November.
